probes.description: Three series: the sample number, a wave between 0 and 100, and a rate that follows it.
probes.label: Synthetic metrics

probes.description: A snapshot table whose rows move on by one id per sample, so rows leave at the top and arrive at the bottom.
probes.label: Synthetic rows

probes.description: The phase (even or odd) and the sample count.
probes.label: Synthetic status

probes.description: The server at a glance, in one DMV query: SQL Server's CPU (its schedulers' non-preemptive time), runnable tasks, batch requests, compilations and re-compilations per second, and user sessions. Rates use the server's own clock (ms_ticks), and a restart starts them again.
probes.label: Overview

probes.description: A fingerprint of each catalog view the SSIS tree and its documents show, in one query: its row count and a checksum of the columns they show (catalogFingerprints in src/shared/ssis/catalog.ts), over the rows row-level security lets the login see; catalog properties only for a sysadmin or ssis_admin, the only ones who may read them. Object Explorer reloads only what changed, keeping expansion and selection.
probes.label: Catalog changes

sources.description: Generated values for protocol, renderer and smoke tests. It runs no SQL, so any connection id is accepted; a disconnect of that id still ends it.
sources.label: Synthetic

sources.description: SQL Server's own activity, read from server DMVs on the connection's " - Activity Monitor" pool (READ UNCOMMITTED, LOCK_TIMEOUT 1000, DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW).
sources.label: Activity Monitor

sources.description: The SSIS Catalog's views, read on the connection's " - Integration Services" pool in the catalog's database, SSISDB (READ UNCOMMITTED, or READ COMMITTED when the catalog has READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT on; LOCK_TIMEOUT 1000, DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW). Object Explorer holds one per connection while an SSISDB node is open. A catalog that no longer exists ends it (CATALOG_MISSING).
sources.label: SSIS Catalog
